extra.message: User input from request.GET['expr'] is passed directly to eval(). Although __builtins__ is set to {}, Python eval() can still be exploited via introspection of the provided namespace (e.g., accessing __class__, __subclasses__) to achieve arbitrary code execution.

User input from request.GET['host'] is concatenated directly into an OS command string passed to os.system(): _os.system("ping -c 1 " + host). An attacker can inject arbitrary shell commands using characters like ;, |, &&, or $(...).

User input from request.GET['fragment'] is passed directly into Jinja2 Template() and rendered: Template("Result: " + fragment).render(). This allows Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI), which can be exploited to read files, execute code, or access environment variables via Jinja2's object traversal.

XML parser is created with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False, and user-supplied request.body is parsed with etree.fromstring(). This allows XML External Entity (XXE) attacks to read local files, perform SSRF, or cause denial of service.

cwe: CWE-611: Information Exposure Through XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: User-supplied JSON from request.body is used directly as a MongoDB query filter: find_one(query). An attacker can inject MongoDB query operators like {"$gt": ""} to match all records or {"$where": "..."} for NoSQL injection.

User input from request.GET['name'] is used directly in path construction (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name) and then arbitrary request.body data is written to that path via target.write_bytes(request.body). An attacker can use path traversal (e.g., name=../../etc/cron.d/malicious) to write arbitrary files anywhere on the filesystem.

User input from request.GET['copyline'] is concatenated directly into an HTML string: "

" + copyline + "

...". The response is served as text/html, allowing cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks.

User input from request.GET['lane'] or request.POST['lane'] is passed directly to redirect(lane), allowing open redirect attacks. An attacker can craft a URL that redirects users to an arbitrary external domain, useful for phishing.

The Origin header from the request is reflected directly into the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header, and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is set to "true". This allows any origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests, effectively bypassing the same-origin policy.

The patient_identity_ping_339 view has no authentication check (no _wrk_gate() call, no @login_required decorator). It is publicly accessible and reflects user-supplied handle and channel parameters back in the response.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: User-controlled JSON from request.body is parsed and used to update a dictionary via workset.update(change_set), allowing an attacker to override any field including security-sensitive ones like is_admin and role. This is an insecure deserialization / mass assignment vulnerability.
Hardcoded verification codes are stored in source code: known = {"north": "4812", "south": "5930"}. These are used as authentication secrets for the patient_identity_hint_459 endpoint.

The patient_care_roll_042 endpoint returns hardcoded sensitive data including a sync_key ("tok_live_partner_sync") that appears to be a live API token, and a tax reference number ("739-44-1982"). Exposing these in an API response risks credential leakage.
The full request body and Authorization header are logged via logger.warning(). This can expose sensitive data such as bearer tokens, API keys, or personal health information in application logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The response explicitly disables XSS protection (X-XSS-Protection: 0) and removes Content Security Policy (Content-Security-Policy: ""), removing browser-level defenses against XSS attacks.
An HTTPS request is made using ssl._create_unverified_context(), which disables SSL certificate verification. This allows man-in-the-middle attacks on the connection to the partner endpoint.

Authorization in patient_badge_gate_529 is based on a cookie value (ops_badge) or header (x-ops-badge) that is entirely client-controlled. If the value is "lead", elevated access is granted. An attacker can simply set the cookie or header to "lead" to bypass authorization.

User input controls both amount and state in a ledger object. An attacker can set state to "approved" and amount to any value, manipulating the balance calculation and bypassing any business logic validation that should govern state transitions.

cwe: CWE-841: Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow

extra.message: The Django SECRET_KEY falls back to a hardcoded default value "dev-only-change-me" when the DJANGO_SECRET_KEY environment variable is not set. This key is used for cryptographic signing of sessions, CSRF tokens, and password reset tokens. An attacker who knows this key can forge sessions and bypass CSRF protection.

DEBUG mode defaults to True (os.environ.get("DJANGO_DEBUG", "1") == "1"). When DEBUG is enabled, Django exposes detailed error pages with stack traces, local variables, and settings (including SECRET_KEY), and serves media files without authentication.

The availability_api endpoint accepts an API key via request.GET.get("api_key"), transmitting the key in the URL query string. This exposes the key in server access logs, browser history, proxy logs, and Referer headers.

cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information

extra.message: User input from request.GET['marker'] is set as a cookie value via response.set_cookie("portal_crumb", marker) without validation or sanitization. While Django's set_cookie encodes values, unvalidated user input in cookies can be exploited for session fixation or stored XSS if other parts of the application trust this cookie value.
